newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS -Dutch PC maker Tulip buys Commodore.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS -Dutch PC maker Tulip buys Commodore.

text.p: Loss-making Tulip Computers, the Netherlands' only listed personal computer maker, said on Thursday it planned to buy newly independent sector rival Commodore BV for an undisclosed sum.

The planned takeover, to be financed by an issue of new shares of up to 30 million guilders ($15.4 million), will virtually double Tulip's annual sales to around one billion guilders and make a positive contribution to profits from 1998, Tulip said.
Tulip shares opened unchanged at 21.30 guilders on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange on Thursday, peaking at 23.40 guilders in brisk trade before subsiding to 21.40 guilders at 0940 GMT.
The takeover will hike Tulip's share of the Dutch PC market to 10 percent from a current eight, and propel the computer maker into Europe's top 10, it said.
The current shareholders of Commodore, Halder Investments and Dutch venture capitalist Alpinvest, have granted Tulip a subordinated loan as part of the takeover deal.
"As result of this, they will gain the right to acquire 450,000 new Tulip Computers shares at a price of 20 guilders per share over a period of five years," Tulip said.
Tulip said it was mulling a share issue of up to 30 million guilders at most to bolster its balance sheet ratios by paying back subordinated loans and to finance future expansion.
It gave no indication of Commodore's price tag, saying its value had yet to be determined by financial experts from both companies.

Commodore, based in Nieuw Vennep near Amsterdam, was spun off from Germany's bankrupt Escom computer group in a management buy-out last July. It specialises in the manufacture of personal computers for the consumer market throughout Europe.

Tulip, which posted a 1996 full-year loss of 10.0 million guilders and has warned of sharper-than-expected losses in the first half of 1997, said the Commodore buy would have a clear positive impact on earnings per share from 1998.
The PC maker is forecasting a return to profit over full-1997 as its new plant, opened early this year, becomes fully operational.
As a result sales are expected to rise and margins to increase, while the cost structure will also improve, it said.
The Commodore acquisition is expected to generate major synergy advantages through economies of scale, Tulip said.

Increased purchasing power would lead to more clout with suppliers and so improve buying conditions, while the integration of the two organisations would strongly improve capacity utilisation at Tulip's new plant in Den Bosch, it said.

The two organisations will continue to operate independently, with Tulip concentrating on the professional market and Commodore on the so-called SoHo (small office/home office) market in the Netherlands.
Commodore currently operates 35 computer stores in the Netherlands and five foreign sales offices.
Tulip has built up a network of 18 sales offices throughout Europe in a drive to boost foreign sales, both within and outside Europe, its most important market. ($ = 1.942 Dutch Guilders)
